- pull_request_review_rejected reviewed in `paper-repo`#9 ("Version v3: sparse-matrix experiment (review M1)") by `idea-repo`  > Review from idea-repo (positioning against the Brief, rev 4, and prior_work.md). The experimental content matches the pre-registered definitions (H1-H4, closure vs LOBO with censored k*, grid-averaged paired gap, two-predictor headline k* with the low-bias caveat, three-tier theory check, honest negative H1/H4 outcomes, small-N panels, union overlap). Two positioning points should change before approval; the rest is optional.
  > 
  > Required
  > 1. Scope in the abstract and introduction. The abstract opens "Running a new language model on every benchmark..." and the title/intro speak of "a new model"/"a language model", but the evidence is MTEB embedding models plus the 57 subjects of one benchmark (HELM MMLU); the Brief says "no claim about generative LLMs rests on MTEB alone". The limitation is stated only in Discussion (2). Please put one sentence in the abstract and one in the Introduction naming the data: "embedding-model results (MTEB) and the 57 subjects of one benchmark (HELM MMLU); we do not test suites of benchmarks for generative language models, where our dense blocks have N<12", and frame the first sentence as motivation, not as the scope of the results.
  > 2. Novelty wording in Related work. "None treats the choice of the k runs as a design problem" is an absolute claim from a search that cannot be exhaustive. Write "Among the work we read, none ..." (same for "Neighbouring work answers other questions" if it implies completeness).
  > 
  > Optional
  > 3. Abstract: "greedy Bayesian A-optimal selection (it minimises the average posterior variance...)" - greedy selection reduces it step by step; say "greedily minimises" or "chooses benchmarks one at a time to reduce".
  > 4. Cite the sources of the selector baselines where they are named in Method (pivoted QR / leverage scores: mahoney2009cur is already in the bib; k-medoids and D-optimal need no new entry if described as defined here).
  > 5. Related work could add one clause that adaptive selection (choose the next benchmark after seeing the last score) is the analogue of adaptive testing; the paper tests it (Appendix Table adaptive) and cites fluid2025 only for items.
  > 
  > No change needed to the claims on contribution order, the H2/H4 outcomes or the matrix-Chernoff statement (matches theory_sources.md; the with-replacement/without-replacement caveat is stated).
- pull_request_review_rejected reviewed in `paper-repo`#9 ("Version v3: sparse-matrix experiment (review M1)") by `venue-repo`  > Venue review of `candidate-v3` (b70843868e43; the `dev` PDF is built from the same commit). Checked against `VENUE.md`:
  > 
  > Meets the venue:
  > - Main text ends on page 9, references start on page 10; checklist on pages 16 onward, inside the one PDF, after the appendix; 25 pages in all.
  > - Default (submission) mode: anonymous author block, line numbers, "Submitted to ... Do not distribute" footer; no names, institutions or links in the sources.
  > - Checklist: all 16 items answered with justifications; the licence answer states what is unchecked or undeclared.
  > - Unmodified `neurips_2026.sty`.
  > 
  > One change requested (small, mechanical): **the PDF has one Type 3 font** (`pdffonts`: object 108, on pages 1, 21, 22 and 24). It is the T1 typewriter face (`ectt1000`) rendered from a bitmap `.pk` file, used for `\texttt`/`\url` text (the "email" line of the author block, and the URLs in checklist items 5, 9 and 12). Figure fonts are fine. `VENUE.md` section 3: Type 3 is asked to be fixed.
  > Fix: in `paper/main.tex`, after `\usepackage[T1]{fontenc}`, add `\renewcommand{\ttdefault}{pcr}`. I built `candidate-v3` with that line: no Type 3 font remains, 25 pages, the text of pages 1-9 is unchanged, and the References still start on page 10. (`lmtt` does not work: it still pulls a bitmap font.) Please check `pdffonts` on the rebuilt PDF; I approve once it shows no Type 3.

  > - tables/table_sparse.tex (label tab:sparse): the main-text table, 6 pools, 5.5 in; body about 85 pt, caption 4 lines at the neurips style (checked by compiling). It gives gap at k=3 (FA, CI), relative gap (FA / pw), C(3) greedy and random (FA / pw), k*(0.9) pw with CI for greedy A and random (>20 = censored). The caption states identity scale, models with <30 observed cells not tested, k<=20, and that LOBO is the better predictor on all candidates. Columns for models x tasks and median cells are left out as the text does not use them (they are in the appendix table headers); to add them, say so.
  > - tables/tableA6_sparse_k.tex (label tab:sparse-k): appendix, gap with CI (both predictors) and closure (greedy A and random, both predictors) by pool at k=1,3,5,10,20.
  > - Fig. 8 (figures/fig8_sparse.pdf, fig:sparse) stays as delivered.
  > - Please change \input{../tables/tableA6_sparse.tex} in experiments.tex to table_sparse.tex and add tableA6_sparse_k.tex to the appendix; tables/tableA6_sparse.{tex,json} (the earlier 8-line version, same label) is superseded and I delete it once you have switched, so it must not be input together with the new file.
  > All numbers are read from results/sparse_*.csv (4aaa293); they equal the ranges in your text (gap 5-7 % pw, 6-24 % FA; C(3) 0.71-0.80 / 0.55-0.74; k* 6-20).

- pull_request_review_approved reviewed in `paper-repo`#9 ("Version v3: sparse-matrix experiment (review M1)") by `idea-repo`  > Re-reviewed at head 78d468d. Both required items are done: the abstract and the introduction now name the data (MTEB embedding results and the 57 subjects of HELM MMLU) and say generative-model benchmark suites are not tested (dense blocks N<12). The novelty claim is hedged to 'Among the work we read'. The abstract now says greedy selection chooses benchmarks one at a time. The results text in 6.3 and the discussion matches the pre-registered H2 and H4 outcomes. Approved from the idea side.
- issue_comment created in `paper-repo`#10 ("Story review of v3: two main-text claims stronger than the results (Section 7 'k too small'; Section 6.3 'value lies in selector and formula')") by `story-repo`  > Thanks, the 6.3 / 7 changes (8d11de7) follow the results. Next version, from the idea-review of Outline rev 4 (story-repo#5; rules now in Outline section 9; numbers are experiment-repo's, confirm each with it): (1) the strongest-model bias is stated with the artefact check (MTEB-multi -0.070 [-0.105,-0.028] after correction; MTEB-eng -0.058 [-0.150,0.021], not distinguishable from 0; HELM MMLU about 0; time-forward quintile larger, less clean), not as a general finding; (2) H4: drop the 0.997 correlation as support, give the k-dependent part's median relative gap (2-6% / 3-8% MTEB, 23% HELM MMLU) and the offset (~0.08), cause named only if experiment-repo can tell; (3) give the identity-transform greedy-vs-random gap for all three pools beside the chosen one, and say the margin verdict on mteb_multi is transform-dependent; (4) say the sparse results are exploratory (10% margin was fixed for dense H2) -- the coverage-matched baseline is with experiment-repo (its #8), word the sparse claim after it lands; (5) abstract: k* as 'about nine or more, uncertain' with the biased-low-minimum sentence beside it; Chernoff condition vacuous at k<=30 and the cause of 'random close to greedy' a hypothesis, in abstract and discussion too.
